scope: An annotated, verified bibliography of the books, academic work, official records and investigations that carry the circulating narratives about money and power in Indian energy and natural resources, plus a calibration of fifteen of those narratives on the six-step ladder. It records what each document actually establishes, who wrote it and with what interest, and what could not be verified. It deliberately does not re-litigate the underlying transactions (coal auctions, PPAs, ALMM, KG-D6), which belong to the sibling domain files; claims here are confined to what the documents themselves record and to the enforcement actions they triggered. Verification was constrained: the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before this sweep began, so verification relied on ~50 direct fetches of publisher, court, regulator and Wikipedia pages; every URL under sources was opened; attempted-but-unopened URLs are in gaps.

claims.d: RIL issued a legal notice on 2014-04-17 demanding withdrawal, destruction of copies and an apology, calling the book defamatory; on 2014-04-23 it demanded ₹100 crore in damages. The authors said the book was balanced and included RIL's perspective.

claims.d: CAG draft report (March 2012) estimated ₹10,673 billion windfall gain to coal-block allocatees for 2004–2009 on a coal-in-situ basis. Superseded by the final report.

claims.lab: CAG final: ₹1.86 lakh cr presumptive gain
claims.d: CAG final report (August 2012) revised the presumptive gain to allocatees to ₹1,856 billion using extractable reserves. PM Manmohan Singh contested the findings, saying government lacked a legal basis to impose competitive bidding unilaterally and faced resistance from coal-bearing states.

benefit.how: Presumptive: allocatees (private and public) obtained blocks without auction; the figure is a counterfactual auction value, not cash paid

claims.d: On 2014-08-25 the Supreme Court held coal-block allocations since 1993 illegal and arbitrary; on 2014-09-24 it cancelled 214 of 218 blocks and imposed ₹295 per tonne on coal extracted from operating mines. The window covers Congress, United Front and NDA-1 governments.

claims.lab: SC closes coal case against Singh
claims.d: In July 2026 the Supreme Court closed the coal-allocation case against former PM Manmohan Singh, accepting CBI closure reports and finding no sufficient material to register corruption charges. Month-level date only.
Prime Minister 2004-05-22→2014-05-26; head of government during the 2004–09 allocations audited by CAG.

On 2023-01-24 Hindenburg alleged a decades-long stock-manipulation and accounting-fraud scheme via 38+ Mauritius shells controlled by Vinod Adani, posed 88 questions and asserted 85%+ downside. The author disclosed a short position.
claims.upgradeIf: SEBI, SC-appointed committee or a court finds minimum-public-shareholding or price-manipulation violations on the offshore-fund facts
claims.killIf: SEBI final orders on all 24 matters find no violation and are not challenged

benefit.how: Gains on a disclosed short position via US bonds and non-Indian derivatives as ~USD 150 bn of market value fell by late Feb 2023

claims.d: Adani Group published a 413-page response calling the report "a calculated attack on India, the independence, integrity and quality of Indian institutions"; Hindenburg replied that Adani had dodged key questions and invited a lawsuit.

On 2024-01-03 a three-judge bench (CJI Chandrachud, Pardiwala, Misra JJ) refused to transfer the Adani probe to CBI/SIT absent "cogent justification indicative of a likely failure of justice"; recorded 22 of 24 SEBI investigations complete and directed the remaining two "preferably within three months"; held third-party reports (OCCRP) "cannot be relied on as conclusive proof"; rejected conflict allegations against the Sapre committee as unsubstantiated.

claims.lab: SC orders probe into Hindenburg conduct
claims.d: The same judgment directed SEBI and Union investigative agencies to probe whether the loss suffered by Indian investors due to Hindenburg's conduct involved any infraction of law, while noting short-selling has legitimate market functions.

claims.lab: OCCRP: offshore funds traded Adani stock
claims.d: In August 2023 OCCRP (with Guardian and FT) reported that individuals and front companies were used to buy and sell Adani stock through Mauritius funds, allegedly bypassing Indian securities law. Original not opened in this sweep.

claims.d: No Adani Group response to the OCCRP report appears in the sources opened here; contemporaneous press recorded a denial, which this sweep did not open. Recorded as a coverage gap, not as silence.
claims.innocentReading: Absence of a captured denial reflects this sweep's source coverage (Wikipedia summaries), not the company's conduct.

claims.d: No Adani response to the coal-grade story appears in the opened sources; recorded as a gap.
claims.innocentReading: Coverage gap in this sweep, not evidence of non-response.

claims.d: On 2024-11-20 the SEC charged Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani and Cyril Cabanes with orchestrating a scheme to pay or promise hundreds of millions of dollars in bribes to Indian officials to secure energy purchase agreements, while Adani Green raised USD 750 m (USD 175 m from US investors) in a September 2021 note offering; EDNY unsealed parallel criminal charges the same day. Press summaries put the alleged bribes at over USD 250 m (≈₹2,100 crore at ~₹84/USD, our conversion).
claims.upgradeIf: Conviction, guilty plea or SEC consent judgment

claims.innocentReading: Coverage gap; the group is presumed to contest the charges.

claims.d: Chairperson of SEBI 2022-03-01→2025-02-28; first woman and first private-sector appointee; succeeded by Tuhin Kanta Pandey (appointed 2025-02-27).

On 2024-08-10 Hindenburg alleged the SEBI chair and her husband held stakes in offshore funds (IIFL-managed) allegedly used in Adani share dealings, implying a conflict of interest in SEBI's Adani probe.
claims.upgradeIf: SEBI board, Lokpal, CVC or a court finds an undisclosed conflict that touched an Adani decision
claims.killIf: Disclosures to SEBI predate the probe and the funds held no Adani exposure while she was chair

claims.d: The Buchs denied the allegations as "baseless", said all disclosures had been furnished to SEBI over the years, and Buch described the report as "character assassination".
In May 2025 the Lokpal dismissed complaints against Buch, citing insufficient evidence and describing the allegations as politically motivated. Month-level date only.

A 2012 CAG audit of Gujarat accused the Modi-led state government of providing low-cost fuel from the state-run gas company to Adani and other businesspeople. Year-level only; the Gujarat CAG report was not opened.
claims.upgradeIf: Gujarat CAG report text opened and the allocation and pricing terms confirmed
claims.killIf: Report shows the pricing was a uniform policy applied to all industrial buyers

benefit.how: Below-market gas from a state PSU during Modi's chief ministership (2001–14), per CAG

claims.d: Adani and Modi have both denied allegations of cronyism (Wikipedia summary; no dated statement captured).
On 2024-02-15 the Supreme Court struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme (notified 2018-01-02) as unconstitutional; SBI disclosed bond data in March 2024.

BJP was the largest recipient of electoral bonds at ₹6,060.51 crore (AITC next at ₹1,609.53 crore) per the disclosures as summarised. Note the ₹9,857 crore total quoted for March 2018–April 2022 is a different window from the party receipts, so the two numbers do not form a clean ratio.

benefit.how: Anonymous (to the public) corporate and individual donations under the scheme

claims.d: The opened summary of the March 2024 disclosures records no documented quid pro quo tying any specific bond purchase to a coal block or energy contract, though three of the top five donors were under ED/IT scrutiny when they bought bonds.
claims.innocentReading: Large infrastructure and mining firms are among the biggest political donors in every democracy with legal corporate donations; co-occurrence of donation and contract is the base rate, not evidence of exchange.

claims.d: The Prime Minister is ex-officio chair of the PM CARES Fund (created 2020-03-27); trustees include the defence, home and finance ministers.

PM CARES is audited by SARC & Associates, not CAG; the government has argued it is not a public authority under RTI while elsewhere describing it as owned and controlled by the Government of India. Receipts: ₹3,076.62 crore (FY20), ₹10,990.17 crore (FY21).
claims.innocentReading: Public charitable trusts routinely appoint private auditors; the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund has the same structure.

claims.d: In 2020 the Supreme Court rejected petitions seeking a CAG audit of PM CARES or transfer of its funds to the NDRF. Month not confirmed in opened source (August 2020 per general record).

claims.lab: SHANTI Act: private entry, supplier liability
claims.d: The SHANTI Bill 2025, passed in the winter session of 2025 and assented, enables limited private participation in nuclear power under regulatory oversight and addresses supplier-liability concerns that deterred GE and Westinghouse; Budget FY26 set a 100 GW-by-2047 target with ₹20,000 crore for SMR development. Exact dates and liability text not confirmed.

benefit.how: Foreign reactor vendors and Indian private developers gain a liability regime and market entry they lacked under CLNDA 2010 s.17(b)

claims.d: Chatterjee (Current History, 2023) frames post-2014 India as oligarchic state capitalism: the state remains pivotal and national champions are instruments of state goals as much as beneficiaries. This is the scholarly alternative to both the "front company" and the "free market winner" readings of Adani.
claims.innocentReading: National-champion policy (Korea, Japan, China) routinely produces a handful of favoured conglomerates without corrupt exchange; concentration is consistent with policy design, not only capture.

claims.d: Mapping Power (OUP 2019; 15 state cases) argues that depoliticised electricity reform fails and durable reform requires a positive dynamic between reform and electoral success; this is the base-rate explanation for chronic discom losses that does not require a villain.
claims.innocentReading: Discom distress is a structural feature of every state regardless of ruling party.

claims.d: Of the twelve books/academic works verified here, the peer-reviewed ones (OUP x2, PUP, CUP, SUP, journal articles) analyse structure and rarely name beneficiaries; the investigative ones (Gas Wars, Feast of Vultures, Billionaire Raj, Hindenburg, OCCRP) name beneficiaries and carry the litigation risk. Readers should not expect the academic corpus to confirm or refute firm-specific allegations.
claims.innocentReading: Different genres answer different questions; silence in the academic literature about a firm is not exoneration.

narratives.claim: Adani is a front for the ruling party (BJP/Modi).
narratives.strongestCase: Documented proximity since Modi's Gujarat years (CAG 2012 on low-cost GSPC gas to Adani and others); extraordinary post-2014 growth in port, airport, coal and renewables awards; a US indictment alleging bribes to Indian state officials; opposition leaders (Rahul Gandhi) repeatedly asserting the link.
narratives.strongestCounter: No court, SEBI, CAG or ED record shows BJP ownership, control or money flow from Adani entities to the party beyond what the bond regime allowed all donors; both Adani and Modi deny cronyism; the Supreme Court (2024-01-03) found no failure by SEBI warranting an SIT; the US indictment names state-level officials and is unproven. Chatterjee's "oligarchic state capitalism" fits the facts without a front-company mechanism: a national champion is an instrument of state policy, which is different from a proxy.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Up to speculative/contested: a documented beneficial-ownership chain or money flow from Adani entities to party-controlled accounts, or a conviction in EDNY naming Union-level actors. Down to debunked: a forensic audit of the offshore funds showing arm's-length third-party capital.
srcs: Indian Kanoon — Vishal Tiwari v Union of India, SC, 2024-01-03
University of Chicago History — Elizabeth Chatterjee

narratives.claim: Ambani and Adani have divided the Indian economy between them by design.
narratives.strongestCase: The two groups rarely compete head-on: Reliance in O2C, telecom, retail; Adani in ports, power, coal, airports, cement; both dominate their sectors and both are Gujarat-rooted; Crabtree's Billionaire Raj documents the concentration of new wealth in a few "Bollygarchs".
narratives.strongestCounter: No agreement, filing or witness has ever been produced; sector non-overlap is the norm for conglomerates that grew from different cores (petrochemicals vs trading/ports); they do compete in renewables/green hydrogen and in city gas (Adani Total Gas vs Reliance-BP), and Reliance took a stake in Adani Power's Mahan project in 2024 as a customer, which is a commercial arm's-length deal, not a carve-up. "By design" is unfalsifiable as stated.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A documented market-sharing arrangement (CCI order, leaked agreement) would move this to contested; continued head-on competition in new energy over 2026–30 would move it to debunked.

narratives.claim: SEBI is captured — the Madhabi Puri Buch conflict of interest.
narratives.strongestCase: Hindenburg (2024-08-10) documented the Buchs' investments in IIFL-managed offshore funds and consultancy income; SEBI took over a year on 24 investigations and two remained open in 2024 pending foreign inputs; ~1,000 SEBI staff protested in September 2024; a Mumbai court ordered an FIR in February 2025.
narratives.strongestCounter: The Buchs denied the allegations as baseless and said disclosures were made to SEBI; the Lokpal dismissed complaints in May 2025 for insufficient evidence; the Supreme Court had already reviewed SEBI's conduct (2024-01-03) and found no "glaring, willful and deliberate inaction"; no order shows a Buch decision that favoured Adani. The staff protest concerned work culture, not Adani.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Up to well-supported: a documented SEBI decision on an Adani matter taken while a Buch-linked fund held Adani exposure. Down to unsupported: the Lokpal record and SEBI's disclosure file being made public and showing no overlap in time.
srcs: Indian Kanoon — Vishal Tiwari v Union of India, SC, 2024-01-03

narratives.claim: Hindenburg was a foreign attack on India.
narratives.strongestCase: Hindenburg is a US firm that profited from a disclosed short; Adani's rebuttal framed the report as an attack on Indian institutions; the Supreme Court did direct a probe into whether Hindenburg's conduct broke Indian law.
narratives.strongestCounter: Short-selling research targets companies, not countries; the report drew on Indian public records (DRI, SEBI, MCA filings); the SC noted short-selling has legitimate functions; Hindenburg published similar reports on US (Nikola), Chinese and European firms and closed in January 2025 with no state actor identified; no Indian agency has published a finding of foreign-state involvement.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A finding by the SC-ordered probe of coordinated market abuse or foreign-state funding would move this to contested.
srcs: Indian Kanoon — Vishal Tiwari v Union of India, SC, 2024-01-03

narratives.claim: The 2025 nuclear liability changes (SHANTI Act) were written for foreign vendors.
narratives.strongestCase: Wikipedia's summary states the Act addresses supplier-liability concerns that had deterred GE and Westinghouse and aims to resolve obstacles to the Indo-US nuclear deal; that is the stated purpose, not a hidden one.
narratives.strongestCounter: "Written for" implies capture; the boring explanation is that CLNDA 2010's supplier right of recourse was an international outlier that stalled all foreign-technology reactors for 15 years, and Indian private developers benefit equally from the same change. The Act also limits, rather than abolishes, recourse (exact text not verified here).
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Section-level comparison of the Act with vendor lobbying positions (US-India Business Council submissions) would settle whether the text tracks vendor asks beyond the international norm.

narratives.claim: Bharat Small Reactors are earmarked for Adani/Reliance.
narratives.strongestCase: Both groups have announced nuclear interest and both are the largest private power/energy investors; NPCIL's BSR model needs deep-pocketed captive users.
narratives.strongestCounter: No allocation, LoI or RFP result naming either group was located (the BSR Wikipedia page does not exist; PIB not opened); the model as announced is user-funded with NPCIL operating, open to all industrial users (steel, aluminium, cement), and Tata, JSW, Vedanta, Hindalco and JSPL are equally plausible takers.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Publication of NPCIL's shortlist or a DAE/PIB release naming selected users.

narratives.claim: ALMM was re-imposed in April 2024 to protect Adani Solar and Waaree.
narratives.strongestCase: ALMM (modules) was suspended for FY2023-24 and re-imposed from 2024-04-01, when Waaree and Adani Solar were the two largest domestic module makers; both gained pricing power in a market otherwise supplied by cheaper Chinese modules.
narratives.strongestCounter: ALMM predates the beneficiaries' scale (order 2019, enforced 2021); the suspension was a one-year concession to developers, and re-imposition restored the status quo; it protects every ALMM-listed maker (Tata Power Solar, Vikram, Premier, dozens of SMEs), not two; the PLI scheme and April 2022 customs duties are the same industrial policy; developers, not Chinese firms, were the rivals who lost. Not verified against MNRE notifications in this sweep.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Share of ALMM-listed capacity held by Adani+Waaree at re-imposition (if >50%, the protection is de facto concentrated); file notings on why the suspension ended when it did.

narratives.claim: Electoral bonds were pay-to-play for coal blocks.
narratives.strongestCase: BJP received ₹6,060.51 crore; several top donors are mining/infrastructure firms (Megha, Vedanta, Essel Mining per press); three of the top five donors were under ED/IT scrutiny when buying bonds; the Reporters' Collective coal series alleges tailored auction outcomes.
narratives.strongestCounter: No dated donation→block sequence has been documented in the opened sources; coal auctions since 2020 are e-auctions with published bids; the biggest single donor (Future Gaming) is a lottery firm with no coal interest; donations by large infra firms are the base rate everywhere. The SC struck down the scheme for opacity, not on a finding of quid pro quo.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A matched timeline (bond purchase date, auction date, winner) across all 2020–24 coal auctions with a control set of non-donor winners.

narratives.claim: The 2022 coal-import blending mandate was designed to benefit Adani.
narratives.strongestCase: Adani Enterprises is India's largest coal importer and trader and operates the largest coal-handling ports; a mandate to blend imported coal raised import volumes; the FT/OCCRP 2024 story alleges grade inflation on imports.
narratives.strongestCounter: The mandate followed the April–May 2022 coal-stock crisis at thermal plants and applied to all gencos; Coal India, Tata, JSW and state gencos also imported; the mandate was withdrawn as stocks recovered. No file noting or committee finding of design intent was located; PRS lists no committee report on it.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Import-volume shares by trader for FY23 versus FY22 (if Adani's share rose disproportionately) and the Ministry of Power file trail.
srcs: PRS Legislative Research — Standing Committee report summaries

narratives.claim: The KG-D6 gas price hike was a gift to Reliance.
narratives.strongestCase: CAG 2011 documented PSC violations and a single-bid USD 1.1 bn contract; the 2013 Rangarajan formula would have roughly doubled the administered price while RIL's output was falling short; Gas Wars documents the ministerial churn.
narratives.strongestCounter: Any administered-price increase benefits every producer (ONGC and OIL produce far more gas than RIL); the 2014 government deferred and then replaced the formula with a lower price (USD 5.61) and imposed output-shortfall penalties; RIL sued the authors rather than the auditor. Rangarajan/Kelkar details were not confirmed in opened sources.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Quantifying RIL's share of incremental revenue under each formula versus ONGC's; cabinet notes on the 2013 decision.
srcs: Wikipedia — Gas Wars: Crony Capitalism and the Ambanis

narratives.claim: Chinese solar cells enter India via ALMM loopholes.
narratives.strongestCase: ALMM List-I covered modules only until List-II for cells took effect (June 2026); Indian module assembly relied overwhelmingly on imported (mostly Chinese) cells and wafers, so "Made in India" modules contained Chinese cells by design of the rule, not by evasion.
narratives.strongestCounter: "Loophole" mis-describes a phased policy: List-II was announced years ahead; DCR tenders already required domestic cells. Not verified against MNRE notifications in this sweep.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Customs data on cell imports after June 2026; whether List-II enforcement was again deferred.

narratives.claim: PM CARES is a slush fund.
narratives.strongestCase: Not CAG-audited; donors undisclosed; government took contradictory positions on RTI status; ₹14,000 crore received in two years with roughly two-thirds unspent by the last figures summarised; PSUs and employees were channelled into donating.
narratives.strongestCounter: Audited accounts have been published (SARC & Associates); large documented outlays on ventilators, oxygen plants and vaccine development; the SC rejected petitions for CAG audit/NDRF transfer; the PMNRF has had the same structure since 1948 under Congress governments. "Slush fund" implies diversion, and no diversion has been documented.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Donor list disclosure or a CAG audit; evidence of spending outside the stated objects.

narratives.claim: The Congress-era coal allocations were the real scam.
narratives.strongestCase: CAG (August 2012) put the presumptive gain to allocatees at ₹1.86 lakh crore for 2004–09; the Supreme Court held every allocation since 1993 illegal and arbitrary and cancelled 214 blocks; a screening-committee process without auction is documented, and convictions of individual officials and politicians followed in trial courts.
narratives.strongestCounter: The SC finding covers 1993–2010 and therefore NDA-1 (1998–2004) as well; the ₹1.86 lakh crore is a counterfactual not a theft; the PM's case was closed by the SC in July 2026 for want of material; the government's defence (states resisted auctions) is on record. "Real" scam is a comparative claim that needs the post-2015 auction record as the control.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Down to contested if the trial-court convictions are reversed on appeal; strengthened if appellate courts uphold them.

narratives.claim: The Supreme Court's 2024 Adani judgment was a clean chit.
narratives.strongestCase: The court refused SIT/CBI, found no deliberate inaction by SEBI, rejected reliance on OCCRP-type reports and dismissed the conflict allegations against the expert committee; it also ordered a probe into Hindenburg.
narratives.strongestCounter: The court explicitly did not adjudicate the merits of the allegations; two investigations were still pending; it directed government and SEBI to act "constructively" on the Sapre committee's regulatory recommendations, which is not an exoneration of the company.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: The content of SEBI's final orders (reported September 2025; not opened here).
srcs: Indian Kanoon — Vishal Tiwari v Union of India, SC, 2024-01-03

narratives.claim: The critical literature is uniformly partisan and therefore worthless.
narratives.strongestCase: Most trade books here (Patel, Baru, Crabtree, Joseph, Guha Thakurta) are written by declared critics of incumbent power; several authors have been sued or investigated.
narratives.strongestCounter: The peer-reviewed corpus (OUP, PUP, CUP, SUP, journal articles) is methodologically conservative and largely avoids firm-specific allegations; the strongest firm-specific records (CAG 2011/2012, SC 2014, SEC 2024) are official, not journalistic; partisanship affects framing, not the existence of the underlying records.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: Nothing would make the genre distinction disappear; the corrective is to cite official records for facts and books for framing.
srcs: OUP — Business and Politics in India (ToC)

symmetryCheck: Control: apply the identical lens (audit → book → legal reprisal → allegation of a favoured national champion) to Reliance under the UPA (2004–14) instead of Adani under the NDA (2014–). It produces the same shape: a CAG audit (KG-D6, 2011) documenting PSC breaches; an investigative book (Gas Wars, 2014) alleging ministers were moved to suit the firm; a ₹100 crore defamation demand; an opposition (AAP/BJP at the time) narrative of "Ambani's government". Two asymmetries are findings about the institutions rather than the firms: (1) under UPA the damaging primary records were produced by domestic institutions (CAG 2011, CAG 2012, SC 2014), whereas under NDA the damaging primary records on Adani are foreign (Hindenburg, OCCRP/FT, SEC/DOJ) and the domestic institutions (SEBI, SC, Lokpal) have so far produced records that cut the other way; (2) the coal cancellation of 2014 covered NDA-1 allocations too, so the "Congress scam" narrative survives only because the volume of 2004–09 allocations was larger, not because the process differed. Applied to a third control — Tata, JSW and Vedanta, who also won ports, airports, coal and renewables under both governments — the lens generates no comparable literature, which says the literature follows the two largest promoters rather than the policy instruments.
